title: Opinion bubbles in the quantum Buridan's ass problem
authors: Leonid Chaichenets, Jaroslav Novotný, Igor Jex, Stephen M. Barnett, Tamás Kiss
abstract: The quantum Buridan's ass problem concerns a network of interconnected nodes in which transitions between the nodes are governed by the laws of quantum mechanics. In such situations interference between probability amplitudes plays a key role in determining whether the probability of leaving the initial node is large or small and also the speed at which the associated transitions occur. In this paper we extend this idea to consider transitions between one given set of coupled nodes and the remainder of the network. We have in mind a quantum analogy to changing an opinion, in which the initially occupied set of nodes is one opinion bubble, with the remaining parts of the network corresponding to a different opinion. We find that quantum interference again plays a crucial role in the dynamics. A further key component is the role of symmetry between the nodes and their interconnections, as it is symmetry that lies at the heart of the Buridan's ass puzzle. In the classical Buridan's ass paradox it is symmetry between competing alternatives that freezes the ass into indecision. In the quantum case, however, interference results in a far richer dynamics.
summary: This theoretical paper models opinion change using a quantum network analogy, treating two coupled subgraphs as 'opinion bubbles.' It shows that quantum interference governs the transition dynamics, predicting that perfect oscillation (avoiding commitment) occurs under specific symmetry conditions, while asymmetry leads to trapping.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the quantum dynamics of excitation transfer between two coupled subgraphs, drawing an analogy to the classical Buridan's ass paradox regarding indecision.
main_result: Quantum interference plays a crucial role, leading to oscillatory dynamics, and full oscillations occur when the symmetry condition ($d_A a = d_B b$) is met, contrasting with classical expectations.
method: The analysis uses the single-photon subspace of a quantum network Hamiltonian, calculating the time evolution of the transfer probability using the Schrödinger propagator.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum network modeled by a Hamiltonian with a block-structured weighted adjacency matrix, representing two coupled regular subgraphs (opinion bubbles).
key_observables: Transfer probability $P_{A 	o B}(t)$, minimal return probability $P_{A	o A}(t)$, and the oscillation frequency $\omega$.
important_parameters: The geometric parameter $\eta$, which relates internal coupling strengths to inter-bubble coupling, dictates the dynamics.
main_assumptions: The analysis is primarily restricted to the evolution of a single photon in the Schrödinger picture, although the Hamiltonian structure allows for multi-excitation study.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate graph structures (e.g., two subgraphs coupled by links) and depict the time evolution of the minimal return probability for various coupling regimes.
paper_structure: The paper extends previous work on single-node evolution to two coupled subgraphs, deriving the time-dependent transfer probability, establishing conditions for full oscillation versus trapping based on symmetry, and discussing asymptotic behavior.
why_interesting: It provides a rich quantum mechanical framework for modeling decision-making or opinion dynamics, showing how quantum interference fundamentally alters classical paradoxes.

In the current paper this situation is generalized to two regular subgraphs (red and blue nodes) having uniform coupling strength within themselves (red and blue edges) and uniformly coupled to one another (black edges). This allows us to cover a number of interesting situations beyond those considered originally.
